item.title: Elder Lakuṇṭaka-Bhaddiya: “Outside the parks, At the Ambāṭaka woodland, In the forest with its groves, Having abandoned craving, the root of craving, Bhaddiya sits in…
item.description:
Elder Lakuṇṭaka-Bhaddiya:

“Outside the parks,
At the Ambāṭaka woodland,
In the forest with its groves,
Having abandoned craving, the root of craving,
Bhaddiya sits in meditation —
Blissful, happy.”

Some people delight
In drums, flutes, and cymbals.
But I, at the root of a tree,
Delight in the Buddha’s teaching.

If the Buddha grants a gift,
I receive that gift.
I bear mindfulness of the body,
Constantly in all realms.

Those who mock me for my body,
Or follow me for my voice —
They do not know me,
Driven by sensual desire.

Not knowing the inside,
Not seeing the outside —
Blocked on all sides, the fool
Is carried away by words.

Not knowing the inside,
But seeing the outside —
Seeing only the external fruit,
He too is carried away by words.

Knowing the inside with wisdom,
Seeing the outside as well —
Seeing without obstruction,
He is not carried away by words.

From: Theragāthā 7.2
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, one who delights in the eye delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights…
item.description:
“Monks, one who delights in the eye delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights in the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … the mind delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. And, monks, one who does not delight in the eye does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering. One who does not delight in the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … the mind does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.19

item.title: “Monks, for direct knowledge of craving, ten things should be developed. What ten? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of disgust…
item.description:
“Monks, for direct knowledge of craving, ten things should be developed. What ten? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of disgust with food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation. For direct knowledge of craving, monks, these ten things should be developed.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.237

item.title: “Monks, there are these five mental shackles. What five? Here, monks, a monk is not free from lust, desire, affection, thirst, fever, craving for sensual…
item.description:
“Monks, there are these five mental shackles. What five? Here, monks, a monk is not free from lust, desire, affection, thirst, fever, craving for sensual pleasures. Monks, for a monk who is not free from lust … craving for sensual pleasures, his mind does not incline to exertion, commitment, persistence, striving. If one’s mind does not incline to exertion, commitment, persistence, striving, that is the first mental shackle.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.206
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “And how, monks, is a monk called an arahant? He has made distant evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing…
item.description:
“And how, monks, is a monk called an arahant? He has made distant evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is an arahant.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 39 – Mahāhatthipadopamasutta

item.title: “Monks, when the child grows up and his faculties become mature, he enjoys the five strands of sensual pleasure fully: forms cognizable by the eye…
item.description:
“Monks, when the child grows up and his faculties become mature, he enjoys the five strands of sensual pleasure fully: forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing; sounds cognizable by the ear … odors cognizable by the nose … tastes cognizable by the tongue … tangibles cognizable by the body that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. When he sees a form with the eye, he lusts after a pleasing form and dislikes a displeasing form. He dwells with mindfulness not established on the body, with a limited mind. He does not know as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom where those evil, unwholesome states cease without remainder. Thus, in relation to the body, whichever feeling arises — pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — he delights in that feeling, welcomes it, and clings to it. Because he delights, welcomes, and clings, delight in sensual pleasure arises. With delight in sensual pleasure, there is clinging. With clinging as condition, becoming; with becoming as condition, birth; with birth as condition, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Thus is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 38 – Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhayasutta

item.title: Suffering from disease and aging, And also subject to death — Such is the nature of conditioned things, Such is the nature of beings. If…
item.description:
Suffering from disease and aging,
And also subject to death —
Such is the nature of conditioned things,
Such is the nature of beings.
If ordinary people become disenchanted,
That would not be fitting for me —
If I too were disenchanted
With beings who share the same fate.
While I live,
Not different from them,
I dwell thus,
Knowing the Dhamma without attachment.
Conceit in health,
In youth, in life —
All these I have subdued,
Springing from security.
I see the path of seclusion,
I arouse strong energy,
Seeing the state of Nibbāna.
Now I cannot
Enjoy sensual pleasures —
I will not fall back,
Achieving the final goal of the holy life.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.57
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Rāhula: Blinded by sensual desires, Covered by the net of wrong views, Craving acts as a veil, Covering, hiding completely. Bound by heedlessness, Like…
item.description:
Elder Rāhula:

Blinded by sensual desires,
Covered by the net of wrong views,
Craving acts as a veil,
Covering, hiding completely.
Bound by heedlessness,
Like a fish caught in a net.

I have overcome those sensual desires,
Cut Māra’s bondage.
Having pulled out the root of craving,
I am cooled, at peace.

From: Theragāthā 4.8
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When…
item.description:
“Monks, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a basis, there is an establishment of consciousness. When consciousness is established and grows, there is a production of future renewed existence. When there is future renewed existence, future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.38
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: "When the eye sees a form, the monk does not grasp the general feature, does not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the…
item.description:
"When the eye sees a form, the monk does not grasp the general feature, does not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the eye faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise — that cause the monk restrains, guards the eye faculty... By means of this noble restraint of the faculties, he experiences an internal feeling of ease, unblemished."

From: Dīgha Nikāya 2 – Sāmaññaphalasutta
